title: Investigate a spreading incident
scenario: Support reports that a three-product catalog is slow or unavailable, although only one lamp dependency branch has been faulted. A facilitator seeds either slow lamp Inventory or disconnected lamp Shipping. Diagnose whether shared workers or aggregate error propagation explains the wider customer impact.
why: The visible failures can be healthy products downstream of a shared bottleneck or an all-or-nothing response. Fixing the wrong dependency or enabling fallback without an appropriate timeout can leave the real problem active.
reproduce: Ask a partner or facilitator to seed exactly one incident from docs/facilitator.md. They keep the chosen dependency and fault secret. Do not inspect Network Faults before writing your hypothesis.
ready: Start with “Clear all faults” and “Restore default settings” in Network Faults. Use the start launcher so fixed background traffic is running. In Storefront, compare the three-product catalog and its worker indicators. Keep the same traffic throughout, use fresh 60–90-second windows, and record changes in the cumulative rejected count rather than its lifetime total. Record the healthy baseline before your partner seeds the incident; do not clear it afterward. This challenge requires another person.
assignment: Which lamp dependency is faulty, how does its impact spread to healthy products, and which mitigation contains that mechanism?

tasks.title: Arrange one hidden incident
tasks.instruction: From a clean baseline, ask a partner to seed Assignment 3. Leave the exact fault secret and keep supplied traffic fixed. Write an abort condition.

tasks.title: Collect the customer symptoms
tasks.instruction: Compare availability and delivery catalog views. Record catalog times/statuses, chair/desk usefulness, active workers, queue state, and the rejected-count change with timestamps. Leave fault controls unopened.

tasks.title: Write a supported diagnosis
tasks.instruction: Use dependency outcomes/latency, product latency, and worker/queue charts. Predict the faulty dependency and whether the impact spreads through shared capacity, aggregate failure, or both. Record an alternative explanation before inspecting controls.

tasks.title: Confirm and contain the mechanism
tasks.instruction: Inspect Network Faults with the facilitator after recording your hypothesis. Apply a justified timeout/fallback setting. For slow calls use a short timeout plus fallback/breaker; for immediate disconnection use an honest partial quote. Preserve the exact original fault.

tasks.title: Validate the healthy products and reveal
tasks.instruction: Retest the same catalog views and fresh windows. Compare healthy product usefulness, queue pressure, catalog time/status and the affected product’s uncertainty. Ask for the reveal and compare it with your hypothesis. Clear all faults, restore default settings, wait for in-flight work and any 5-second cooldown, then verify all three products have live stock and delivery information. Submit your own measurements.

done: You recorded a diagnosis and propagation mechanism before inspecting fault controls.
You retested the identical incident and showed which healthy-product or catalog outcome improved, while recording the affected product’s missing data.
You compared the diagnosis with the reveal and restored all three products.
solution: Slow Inventory can increase latency in both catalog views and occupy shared workers. Chair/desk latency or rejection signals can worsen despite healthy dependency branches.
Disconnected lamp Shipping should fail delivery aggregation but leave availability working. It can fail fast without filling the worker queue.
A short timeout bounds slow worker occupancy; the breaker pauses repeated failed product calls; fallback preserves honest partial catalog results. Choose the combination supported by the evidence.
Validate under the same fault and traffic. State which signals improved and which information remains unavailable, then restore and verify all products.

fields.label: Customer symptom and time window
fields.prompt: Which customer route is slow or failing? When did you observe it?

fields.label: Grafana evidence
fields.prompt: Which dependency and signals changed? Include panel names and your observations. A Prometheus query is optional.

fields.label: Hypothesis and uncertainty
fields.prompt: What is the likely fault? What else could explain the evidence?

fields.label: Mitigation and reason
fields.prompt: What did you change, and why does it address this symptom? Distinguish the roles of timeout, circuit breaker and fallback.

fields.label: Validation under the same incident
fields.prompt: Compare the same route and signals before and after the change. Include all three products, complete-catalog timing/status, worker queue and rejected-count change over the same observation window.

fields.label: Conclusion and cleanup
fields.prompt: What was confirmed? What trade-off remains? Confirm the facilitator removed the incident.

overview.title: 3 · Find how the incident spreads
overview.description: Diagnose a hidden lamp fault from catalog failures, healthy-product impact and real worker indicators.
